units.title: Notice: stairwell lighting, floors 6 to 8 (ref KE/DC/1115)
units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Notice ref KE/DC/1115. Further to previous notices, Kerrow Estates confirms that the intermittent failure of stairwell lighting between floors 6 and 8 is attributable to a faulty timer relay on the riser circuit. A replacement relay has been ordered through the approved procurement route. Storm conditions have delayed the contractor's attendance. There is no evidence of unauthorised access. Kerrow Estates thanks residents for their patience.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: 'Has been ordered.' Last week it was 'requested'. The week before it was 'being sourced'. Next week it will be 'in transit' and the week after that 'awaiting fitting'. I drove buses for thirty-one years, and I know a timetable that isn't one when I see it.

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Thank you for the update. Could you give us even a rough week? I only ask because R. is counting the days to 'when the box man comes', and I'd like to be able to tell him a true number instead of a made-up one.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: For residents: the old thread stays locked. Comments here about the relay and the notice only, please, not about each other. I rang the estates line again at lunch and they could not tell me the contractor's name, so I've written to them asking for it. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Noted, and I'll keep to it. One point on the notice, strictly about the relay: a timer relay fault explains the lights failing. It does not, on its own, explain anything about steps. These are independent questions, and fixing the first will tell us something useful about the second. That is all.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Agree with Tobin, entirely. Once the lights stay on, a recording made under the same conditions as before will tell us more than anything we've argued about. I note my agreement for the record, because he'll enjoy it.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Thank you for the notice. I use the lift now anyway. The lift is also not fixed properly, it stops a little below 8 and you step up, but I prefer it. When the relay is done I will tell you if I go back to the stairs. Maybe.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: tobin and hollis agreeing in public. the storm really has changed everything. next they'll be sharing a spreadsheet. bev, permission to frame this

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: (14.) Small observation about 'no unauthorised access': the riser cupboard on 7 has a new padlock on it since the storm, brass, still shiny. Which is either good maintenance or a very tidy intruder. I'm choosing maintenance, for my own peace of mind and the badger's deadline.

units.title: A note from Ollie's mum
units.author: dc_12_ollie
units.text: Hello everyone, this is Ollie's mum. I've read back through the last few weeks and I'm sorry, Ollie got carried away. He's fifteen and the stairs have become his favourite subject at school. I'm taking the account back. About the roof door: I asked Bev, and the caretaker checks it last thing, and he's sure it's locked at night. Thank you to everyone who answered him kindly, especially Ivy. Carol, 12E

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Thanks, Carol. Ollie's very welcome at the next meeting with you. He asks good questions, which is more than some of the adults manage. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: ollie if you're reading this over your mum's shoulder, respect, you were a legend on here. the roof door is fine mate. come and help me carry water next time there's a storm, you can count the steps

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: (Carol, he's been lovely, honestly. Tell him the drawing of the roof door with him in it is his when I've finished the badger. I've given him a torch and a very serious expression.)

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: love I came in at five off the night bus and the stairs were full of wind from the broken window on 7, it was whistling all the way down like a kettle on the boil, first time I've ever heard a thing on those stairs in eleven years and it was the weather, which I was very grateful for, I'll be honest

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, the wind broke the window on the 7th floor landing at about four this morning. I heard it go. I swept it up at six so that nobody would cut their feet, and put the pieces in a box by the bins marked 'glass'. Thank you, Jordie and Hassan, for the water yesterday. I did not need it, but I have put it under the sink for the next time. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Irena, you swept glass in your slippers on a landing with no lights. Next time please ring the shop. I'll tape cardboard over the frame this morning before the next gusts. Bread is late, the van is stuck behind a tree on the ring road, so it's crackers until lunch. H

units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Notice ref KE/DC/1116. Kerrow Estates is aware of storm damage to the glazing on the 7th floor landing. A temporary boarding contractor will attend when conditions permit. Residents are asked not to attempt repairs themselves. The passenger lift will be returned to service when wind speeds permit.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: The lift came back at 11:20. I took it to the ground floor to look at the bin store. The east side bins have been emptied. All of them. Nobody's lorry could have got into the car park yesterday with the trees down on the ring road, and the private firm says it hasn't been. I would like to know who emptied my bins, so that I can thank them, and also complain to them about the lid.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Wendell, that was the council. They sent a small caged truck round the blocks this morning to clear anything that might blow about, I saw them at seven. The lid was the wind, not them. H

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Irena, thank you for sweeping it. R. noticed the stairwell sounds different with the window out, and he's right, it whistles. He's decided it's a friendly whistle, like a kettle, which is Lorna's word, he heard me read her post out. Little M. says it's the building singing. I'll take either.

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Irena, I wrote to Mr Peake this afternoon, by hand, on the good paper, children first as you said. Lorna, I'll go in with the flask and the colouring book next week if I don't hear. The GP is writing about R.'s sleep. Thank you all. It feels better to be doing something.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Young tern has asked me, privately and very politely, about a file of his from the test night. I shall say here only what I said of my own reel: machines remember, and ears complete. Neither is a ghost. I shall listen to it on proper headphones when he posts it, and say plainly what I hear. Regards, Ned

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thank you, Ned. The tapes have rested two days in the warm, upright, away from the radiator, and one of the cards says 'reservoir dawn, very cold, M. came too'. I'll bring them to Tollinby when the roads open, with the cards, and a cake from my brother's wife, who insists.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Gerald and I made it up to tern's (the ring road was a slalom, but open). The wind has dropped to almost nothing at his house, which is uncanny after yesterday. If the Met's lull holds we'll take Gerald to the road by the pumping house for an hour, just to set levels. Not the session. Headphones on.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Reservoir road's cleared as far as the lay-by; I moved the trees myself with the estate tractor. The dam path is under water at the bottom, so stay on the road. And I'll say this once, since you've been patient with me: the rut's over, and I've not heard deer knock like that at this end of the year, not in thirty years on this estate. I don't know what it is. It's still no reason to be in my woods at night.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thank you, Mr Ashcombe. That means a lot, coming from you, and I won't quote it at anyone. I'm staying home tonight; the dam path's where I'd be and it's under water. Tern and Odile are only setting levels on the road. The session proper starts the first fully calm night, as planned.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Gilliver's flat calm too, for now. The stillness after a big blow always sounds louder than the blow itself. Every halyard in the harbour stopped at once about eight o'clock and you could hear the fish-shed pump from the far end of the wall. It's a pump.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so back. we were on the road by the pumping house 22:10 to 23:00, Gerald on his tripod about 1.6 m up, my H5 next to him for comparison. synced off the logger and clapped. content: drips off every branch, the reservoir lapping, the pumping house motor ticking over, a tawny owl twice. no knocks. no sheep, even. it was lovely, honestly

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on for the playback in tern's kitchen: drips left and right and above, the water behind, the motor low and steady in front. It's like sitting inside a clock. Nothing else at all, which is a result too. Gerald now knows what the road sounds like when nothing's happening.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: That's exactly what we needed: a baseline from the middle position with the binaural head, in still air, before anything else. Thank you both. Please put it in the shared folder labelled as a levels test, not a session file. Make of it what you will.

units.title: test night, 23:53: two knocks and something between them (raw and slowed)
units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so. I said I'd listen properly first. on my pumping house file from the test night, at 23:53:40 there are two dull knocks, 1.4 s apart. between them, much quieter, there's a sound. at normal speed it's a mumble. slowed to 50% it sounds like two syllables. I'm not saying it's a voice. I'm saying I can't make it not sound like one. raw and slowed both in the shared folder. clock synced off the logger, said out loud twice.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Quick analysis, on the raw. The middle sound sits between about 300 and 700 Hz with two broad peaks, which is what slowing does to any short noisy event: it smears energy into bands the ear reads as vowels. The two knocks fit the outflow valve's closing pattern, though I'd want the schedule to be sure. For the middle, a ewe's cough is my favourite candidate. Thanks for posting raw first.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: it's not the sheep. I know what that sheep sounds like, it's on every minute of the file, it's to the right and far off where the field is. this is close and it's in front of the mic. I'm not saying it's anything, hollis, I'm just saying it's not her

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: I've listened twenty times on the raw, on good headphones. On mine, from the dam path, I have the two impacts at the same second, which is the first time our sets have lined up exactly. Between them I hear something short, like a cough, close to tern's mic. I'm not sure it's that either. Make of it what you will.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on, raw file, three times. It's on the left, low, and close, and it doesn't move during the gap. A sheep at the fence would be well off to the right and further away. I'm not saying what it is, and I know Hollis will say a mono recorder can't tell me left from right. This one's stereo, Hollis.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Good thread. Please keep it exactly like this: raw file first, processing second, opinions last. Anyone posting 'it says' followed by a word will have it edited to 'it sounds like'. And nobody re-uploads this anywhere.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: It's a ewe. They cough exactly like an old smoker, I've worked on farms. Failing that, the pumping house has a pressure relief valve that coughs when the main closes, and it'd be close to tern's mic. Either way, not a mystery. A pump or a sheep.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys this is it. this is the one. two syllables between two knocks in the middle of the woods. I'm not reposting it, before anyone starts, but I'm reacting to it on stream tomorrow

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: You can react to whatever you like on your own channel, but you won't play tern's file on it, and you won't describe it as 'the one'. Consider this the same warning as last night, not a new one.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok, fair test. next calm night I'll record the sheep on purpose, same mic, same spot, and post it right next to this one. if her cough matches, I'll say so in one line like hollis does. if it doesn't, I'll also say so. that's all I can do

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Housekeeping. A member has posted about his own past work for a company, which he is entitled to do. Nobody else is entitled to demand the details, guess at the names of his former workmates, or go looking for his family. Several posts doing exactly that have been removed overnight. Please don't make me remove more. Pell (Admin).

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: For the record, since people will ask: I've searched what the northern authorities have online for any clearance consent naming Grieve, and for anything containing 'Corran'. Nothing. But their planning archive isn't digitised before about ten years ago, so that's not evidence it didn't happen. It's evidence their archive isn't online. I'll leave it there.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: He's edited it. The bit about where it was has gone. Why would you take out the location unless somebody got to you overnight? I'm only asking what everyone's thinking.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Or because he realised that a light, a head and a crew of eight is enough to identify him to anyone who knows the area, and he'd rather it wasn't. What would we expect a man to do if he regretted saying too much about himself? Exactly that. People edit posts for ordinary reasons all day.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: 'nobody talks about it'. great. so nothing happened then. a job finished, some blokes went home. there's your mystery

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 6, offered with very low confidence and I'll retract it the moment it's explained: Grieve's published accounts from eight years ago carry an unexplained 'contract dispute provision'. It could be anything. A bad debt. A lorry. A client who didn't pay. I post it only because someone else will find it and make it into something it isn't.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I hope the young man who used to work for them is all right. He sounds like someone who has been carrying something a long time. My father was like that after the war and never said a word either, and we didnt ask him, and I'm still not sure if that was the right thing.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran
units.text: I've had messages. Some from the paper. I'm not answering them, and I'm not being rude. I took the place out because it isn't mine to put up. Some of the lads have families up there. Thank you, Maud. I'm all right. I just didn't want the ones on the Holm thinking they're the first.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: 'Not the first.' Think about that. Not the first island, not the first crew, not the first thirty days. And not the last either, if you know what to look for... I've said more than enough.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect a land speculator to send after an unwelcome article? A warm email with no facts in it, to as many addresses as can be bought, so that the company appears friendly and the story has nowhere to go. That's what arrived. It's dull, not sinister.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: TollinbyMum asked how they got her address. Most likely a bought regional marketing list; I'm on it too, I'm on everything. Finding 7, with good confidence: the 'community information' address isn't registered to Ardent Vale at all, but to a public relations agency in Halvard that handles eleven other clients. So the update was written by people who may never have seen the Holm.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: That fits, and it's the most useful finding on this thread. An agency writing for a client who has told it nothing will produce exactly that email. It also means asking the community desk questions is pointless. Ask the company, in writing, through its registered address. I have.

units.title: Storm clear-up: chainsaw and plant work available
units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Bumping myself with a new post since the old one's sunk. Storm clear-up, fallen trees cut and stacked, fully insured, chainsaw tickets CS30 and CS31, own tipper. Domestic or farm, no job too small. Port ammet, tollinby and brackwater. Pensioners first, at cost. And still keen on subcontract on the Holm if Grieve ever answer their phone.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Moved to Trades & Jobs, where it belongs, with thanks for the pensioners line. Pell (Admin).

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Davey, same as I told you on the quay. Storm trees in Tollinby pay as well and you're home for your tea. The Holm's a long way back in a small boat at the end of a day. Aye, and they've not asked you, which is an answer.

units.title: Day 15 readings: the bottom of it
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Overnight at Carrow Point: lowest pressure 971.4 hPa at 02:06. Peak gust 61 knots at 23:50 last night, on the spare anemometer, which reads low, so the real figure was probably higher. That's a station record. 06:30 now: 983.0 hPa rising fast, wind W 30 knots gusting 46, squally showers. Rain since the start: 61 mm. A lull is forecast tonight before the back end tomorrow.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: see, told you. bit windy, some trampolines. storm of the century my foot. back to normal tomorrow and everyone will have forgotten

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: A small correction for Cal: 61 knots is a record for my station in eleven years, the trampolines were incidental, and it isn't over. The lull tonight is the gap between the low and its trailing trough. Expect the wind back up from about 03:00 and gusting 50 again in the morning. Put the chairs back in the shed.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Out at five to look, in the lull between showers. Inner moorings held bar the two punts we pumped yesterday. The wall's lost three coping stones by the lifeboat house and there's weed and stones the length of the harbour road. My Annie's fine. Nobody's boat is going anywhere today, harbour's still shut.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Lisle: Sound Lines say one sailing at midday 'subject to inspection of the slip'. The office says work from home again. My laptop battery is now my most important relationship. The Lisle shop has run out of milk and is selling powdered milk from a box that may date from the last big storm.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: A small Society note while we all wait for the ferry: the wiki's article on the Gilliver window lamp has been tidied after an edit war overnight. Please don't add 'to ward off spirits' again. None of the 1976 informants says any such thing, and a holiday leaflet is not a source.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Tollinby: school shut again today, open tomorrow they say. Power came back at 11:40, the freezer survived, peas fine, as Garvey promised. I have now played eleven games of a card game I do not understand with a six-year-old who changes the rules every hand. I have lost all eleven. I think that was the point.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: You can see the Holm again this afternoon between the showers. It looks the same from here, long and dark, which I find a comfort, though I couldnt tell you why. I kept the lamp lit all through, and I shall keep it lit tonight. The harbour road is a mess of weed and stones but the lifeboat lads are sweeping it.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Tollinby rd reopened at the garden centre dip, the car's been towed, the crisps man is now a local legend. Lower Tollinby rd at Mill Bridge is shut, the verge has slipped into the beck. Brackwater jct: council have stood the temporary lights back up. Already red. I sat through three cycles for old times' sake.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Walked the estate woods this afternoon. Two oaks down below the dam path, a lot of limbs on the reservoir side, the dam path itself under water at the bottom where the overflow's running. Ridge road's still shut by Holly Lane. Keep out of the woods for now, all of you, daylight included.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: For the record, since some clever clogs on here said the outages were 'Sound Power not maintaining the lines': yesterday was trees. Real ones, with roots. I've got sawdust in my ears to prove it. Brackwater ridge is still off where the two poles are down. We'll have it back tomorrow if the morning gusts behave.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Thirty-one hours, with two sleeps in the van. Tollinby's back, the care home's back, the Brackwater hamlet's back except four farms. Saw a barn owl sitting on a downed pole on the ridge at dusk like it was supervising the job. Garvey says it's the most useful supervisor he's had in years.

units.title: Thank you to whoever waved me round the flood at the garden-centre dip
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: On the worst night, at about nine, I had to fetch my mum's tablets from the late chemist and came to the dip by the garden centre with the water right across. Someone in a hi-vis with a big torch stepped out and waved me round the shallow edge, then back onto the road. Tall chap, long coat, hood up. I didn't get the chance to thank him. If it was you, thank you.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Same spot, same night, I came through about half nine on my last drop and somebody waved me round too, but it was not a tall chap. Short woman, five foot nothing if that, chest waders and a head torch, definitely not a long coat. Waved me round the left side like she'd been doing it for hours. Maybe they took it in turns?

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Not me, before anyone asks, I'm five nine and I was up a sycamore on Chandlers Row all night. Could've been the fire crew, they had a tender at the dip for the crisps man earlier. Or somebody from the garden centre, they live behind it.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Wasn't the fire crew, they'd gone by eight, I spoke to them. I drove through at ten on my way back from the reservoir and there was nobody at the dip at all. Somebody had left a traffic cone on the crown of the road with a torch taped to the top of it, which did the job well enough.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: tall bloke at nine, short woman at half nine, cone at ten. it's the garden centre family taking shifts and then going to bed, lads. mystery solved, you're welcome

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Cal, for once I think you're probably right, and I'll take a box of biscuits round to the garden centre tomorrow to find out. Whoever you are, tall, short or cone: thank you. My mum got her tablets.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Day two of the storm suspension. My recycling box blew off its paving slab in the night and has been found in the council's own Rope Walk Yard, against the sandbag pile, which makes it, I suppose, technically council property. I have asked for it to be collected. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: chandlery open. lost a whole pallet of fenders off the yard to the wind, forty of them, white and blue. if anyone finds fenders on the beach between here and lisle they're mine and there's a pint in it. harbour still shut till the HM says

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Harbour Notice 15/1. Gilliver harbour reopens to essential movements from 10:00. Please check your moorings at low water and report any damage to the harbour office. The slipway remains closed until it has been inspected; there is weed and loose stone on the lower section. Thank you for your patience. HM Quill

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Storm damage on our side, for the record: one deck floodlight smashed by something flying, possibly a roof slate, possibly a gull's lunch, and one bilge pump float jammed with a crisp packet. If anyone wants to argue about which was worse, the bilge alarm went off at 03:00 and I was the one who got up.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: The midday sailing ran, forty minutes late, heavy swell at the Lisle approach but nothing worse. I can't comment on anything Sound Lines hasn't announced, and I'd ask people not to guess. The boat's fine and the crew's fine. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Head office had us in one at a time at the Ammet office this morning for a 'welfare chat' with a woman from personnel with a clipboard. I told her the same as the log, word for word. She was kind. I don't think she knows what it's for either. She asked how many nights in a row I'd done. I told her. She wrote it down twice.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: had mine too. she asked if i was sleeping. i said i'm a deckhand, i sleep when the boat lets me. she wrote something down and underlined it. then she asked if i'd seen anything 'unusual' on the night runs and i said define unusual and she said 'whatever you think' and i didn't really have an answer

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Please note: the Gilliver and Lisle slipways remain closed to the public under Harbour Byelaw 14 until they have been inspected after the storm. That includes walking down to look at the damage, and it includes standing at the end of them. Thank you.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Lisle pier came through all right. The storm took one bulb on the slip lights, the seaward one of course, which leaves the very end darker than ever... ha, anyway, the council electrician says tomorrow. I've brought my big torch to work like a lighthouse keeper and I'm keeping it on the hut windowsill.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Gilliver feeder held all through, not a single trip, which is why the harbour lights never went. One of the old sodium heads on the Gilliver slip is flickering tonight, but that's age, not the storm. Ticket's in with the council. Don't anyone go reading anything into a flickering lamp.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: kit r0we. I know your mother, I know your nan, and I know which chippy you work at. that's your last one on here. kerris has answered every question anyone's asked her straight and she doesn't need the comedy. leave it

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Garvey, a good post, thank you. A genuine question: after a storm like this, how much of the next fortnight's faults turn out to be storm damage showing itself late? Water in joints, cracked insulators, salt? I'd expect a tail of trips, and I'd expect people to blame something else for it.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Aye, there's always a tail. Salt on the insulators after a westerly like that, water in the joints, a cracked pin you don't find till it rains. You'll get trips on and off for a fortnight. That's real corrosion, before anyone quotes me on it later, and it looks like what it is when you go up and look.

units.title: Monitor 4: new camera fitted today
units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Logged. 15:00 today: the camera feeding monitor 4 replaced, new unit, by IT and a contractor. Same pole, same corner of the stack yard. IT confident this ends the 'figure at the edge of the lights' entries. I hope so. Old unit is in a box in the hut labelled 'faulty'. Patrolled 00:30, nil found. Will report.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Fingers crossed for a boring night. I'll bring two rolls at four as usual, and an extra one for the IT lad if he's still about, as a reward for optimism.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: This is a good test, as long as you keep notes on what changed and what didn't. If the old entries were a camera fault, they stop. If they were the scene, the lighting or the recorder, they won't. Either answer is useful. I'd be curious what you find.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: For comparison, Gate7: when Control replaced our camera at the retail park entrance last spring, the 'ghost car' that kept appearing at the barrier went with it. Turned out the old one had a burnt-in image from years of the same view. So it does happen. Hope yours is that.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Thanks, Dev. Burnt-in image is a good one; I've added it to the list for IT. Patrolled 01:45, nil found. Monitor 4 quiet so far. Rolls collected, one held back for IT.

units.title: A night of storm leftovers, and one thing I'll leave alone
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Mostly storm leftovers tonight: a roofer with a wrist, two cyclists, an old fella who went out to look at the sea and met it. My mate on the porters' bank tonight used to cut trees for a living. Somebody in the rest room was reading out the Sound Board thread about the island job, and he got up and went to do a linen run that wasn't due for an hour. Didn't say a word. He's a good lad. Leaving it there.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Leaving it there is a kindness. Some jobs leave people in a room they don't come out of easily, and the worst thing is someone reading the door sign aloud. Tell him, if it's ever useful, that a bookshop in Tollinby has a chair by the stove and no questions.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping, gently: please don't bring other forums' arguments about named companies into Lamp Hours, and please don't read them aloud to colleagues in rest rooms. This is for company on the night shift. Thank you for leaving it there.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: love the depot had every bus in it last night nose to tail like sardines, I mopped round forty-one of them and one of the drivers slept on the back seat of the 14 because he couldn't get home over the bridge, I left him a tea on the step, the wind was howling in the wash bay doors like a choir

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: Second storm night: the generator ran the whole shift, and management dropped the rate to 120 'due to environmental conditions'. Never thought I'd be grateful to a storm. Yard still full of trailers. Half the day shift couldn't get in, so we're doing their lines as well, at the lower rate, which is a kind of maths.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: The pet shop's trolley bay roof has been found. It was in the drive-through lane of the burger place across the ring road, flat, like it had queued. Control has requested a written report on 'trolley bay roof displacement'. I've written 'wind'. It's a short report.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Small corridor news: Rufus walked to the corner of the back corridor tonight, sniffed for a long time, turned round and came back. That's further than he's gone in a fortnight. Either it's progress or a new opinion. Biscuit didn't bother sniffing and went straight past him, which is very her.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: chapter 3 has a figure in it now. the figure is a bar chart. it is the most beautiful bar chart that has ever been made and my supervisor said 'fine'. I'm taking 'fine'. going home before 4 for once, the corridor lights came on for me and only me

units.title: Ward 9, storm edition
units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Halvard missed the worst of your storm, but we got some of its patients by air ambulance: two from the Sound coast with chest infections after a cold night with no heating. One kept asking what time the ferry was. I said there's no ferry here, love, you're in Halvard. He said 'there's always a ferry' and went to sleep. Back to it.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: picked up two of your doctors at the hospital rank at four, they slept the whole way across town, one was holding a sandwich like it was a baby, I didn't wake him at the lights, anyway the fare was on the meter and the tip was the sandwich, which I did not take

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: 'There's always a ferry.' Our residents say things like that, and I've stopped correcting them; they're usually right about something, just not about the timetable. Quiet night here. The new junction box has kept its mouth shut and Mrs A. slept straight through.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: The swell has gone as quietly as it arrived. Tonight the sea at the landing is flat enough to see the lamp reflected in it, a second light lying on the water a little way out, which always looks to me as if someone has rowed out to keep the first one company. I suppose it was your storm, reaching us here only as a rumour.

units.title: Storm calls from the other side of the world
units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Our helpline got your storm second-hand tonight. Three customers with family in the Sound rang to ask whether we could check if their mum's power was back. We can't, wrong company, wrong country, wrong ocean. I found the Sound Power outage page on the internet and read it out to them anyway, street by street. The script doesn't cover it. I don't care. (Brb.)

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Hana, that's the nicest thing anyone's done off-script all week. The overnight show had a woman ring from your side of the world to ask the same, about her dad in Brackwater. I read her the co-op's list too. Her dad was back on at 22:10. She cried and then apologised for crying on air. Nothing to apologise for.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: You'll see. When it comes out, and it will, remember who said 'watch what moves while nobody's watching'. I can't be more specific than that... not here.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: closing this thread. Dmitra asked three fair questions and they haven't been answered, and 'I can't say' isn't a conversation. Lamp Hours is company on the night shift, not campfire stories. Drink some water, everyone.

units.title: Back in the cab
units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Wind dropped under the limit tonight, so we're back on night lifts: precast stair cores going up on the hospital extension, one every forty minutes. From 60 m the city looks rinsed clean after yesterday's rain, every streetlight sharp as a pin. Anyone else back at it after the weather? What does your view look like tonight?

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: View from the cage, going down: black, then a lamp, then black, then the station lights at the bottom. Same every night. View from the bus home: the town, frost on the roofs, one bakery lit. Better than yours, if you like bread.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Nobody asked a baker, but here it is. View from my oven door: forty loaves going gold at the edges, and the harbour through the steamed-up window, every boat with its riding light on like a row of candles. I'd swap with nobody.
